lines.text: Private sales, folks! No dealers! No Rex! Just honest people selling honest things! Linda?

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: For sale. One staircase, slightly too long. Takes you one floor further than you need. You will not be told what's on that floor.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: For sale. Hot air balloon. Only flown once. Still flying. Please collect.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Free. One kitten, three eyes, very good at noticing things. Will notice things about you. Will be kind about it.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: For sale. A Grumbel's Ladder, the Ambition model. Selling because I would like to come down now. Please send help. Please send a ladder.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Ooh. I'll take the ladder. Linda, put me down for the ladder.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: It's the Late Lot, folks. The lot's closed. The lights are off. Shh.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: The deals are still on.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Folks. Psst. Over here. Behind the used moons. I've got a deal so good I can't say it out loud. Linda, tell them.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: He's got a toaster.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: It's a very good toaster, folks.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: You know the best thing about the lot at night, folks? The planets are switched off, so you can see the stars. Some of them are for sale.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Most of them aren't. I like those ones best.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Don't tell anyone I said that.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: It's three in the morning. Rex has fallen asleep at the desk, on the cold side.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: For the next few minutes, nothing on this station is for sale.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: This is my favourite part of the night.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Good morning, early birds! It's the Early Bird Specials! Linda, have we got worms?

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: One worm, Rex. It's on layaway.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Early bird special! Buy one sunrise, and get the rest of the morning free! Linda?

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: The rest of the morning was already free, Rex.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: And now it's a deal!

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: We've had a call from the one actual bird again, folks! He'd like a worm. We don't sell worms, buddy! But I've got a lovely birdhouse with a sea view!

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: It's a shoebox, Rex.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: A shoebox with a sea view!

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: This is Linda's Hour. For the next sixty minutes, the small print will be read at a normal speed. Please make yourselves comfortable.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Linda, the clock is ticking!

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Not in my hour, Rex.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Welcome back to Linda's Hour. Here is some small print that isn't attached to anything.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Results may vary. Past performance is no guarantee of future results. Your journey may differ.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: I just think they're lovely sentences. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: A listener has asked what I do on my day off. I read the terms and conditions of things I will never buy. Slowly. With a cup of tea.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Nobody has ever read them before me. Somebody should.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Linda, a quick one! Can I just do one ad?

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: No, Rex.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: It's a really good chair!

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: It's my hour, Rex. You can sit in the chair. Quietly.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: It is a good chair.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Folks! A slightly used ocean! One previous owner, a whale who has moved on! It's wet! It's deep! It comes with waves!

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Need more space? Get a Bellows Extra Room! It goes in between your other rooms! Nobody knows how! Nobody needs to know how!

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Folks, it's a pre-owned volcano! Only erupted once, and very politely! Perfect for barbecues! Perfect for drama!

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Tired of Monday? Trade it in! Bellows will take your Monday off your hands and give you a lightly used Sunday evening! It's a little bit sad! It's still the weekend!

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Folks, I've got a cloud! A whole cloud! It's fluffy, it's white, and it follows you home! Never be too hot again!

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Bellows Mystery Keys! Every key opens something! We don't know what! Find out! It's an adventure, on a keyring!

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Folks, it's a gently used tomorrow! Somebody already had it, and they say it was fine! You know what's coming! No surprises! Some surprises!

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Shadow looking a bit short? Bellows Shadow Extensions add a good three feet at four in the afternoon! Look taller! Feel longer!

clips.title: A Clock with a Grandfather in It

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: It's a grandfather clock, folks! It's got a real grandfather in it! He tells the time! He tells you the old days were longer!

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Folks, a staircase that only goes down! Never climb again! Every trip, a happy little descent! Where does it end? Downstairs, folks! Always downstairs!

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Bellows Bottled Sunday Mornings! Uncork one on a Tuesday, and smell the toast, hear the bells, feel the newspaper! Ah!

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Instant friends, folks! Just add water! Six in a packet! A little damp at first, but they dry out, and then they want to go for brunch!

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Product may not be as described. Product may not be described. Product may describe you. Do not let the product describe you. It is very honest, and it has noticed things.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Item sold as seen. Item has not been seen. Item may be glimpsed out of the corner of your eye, late at night, in the kitchen, but never directly. This is normal for the item.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Offer valid until the end of time. The end of time is at the Lounge, Heat Death Boulevard. Please bring your receipt. Barnaby will stamp it, and call it a real heartbreaker.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Rex Bellows is not a licensed anything. Rex Bellows has a licence for something. Nobody knows what. He keeps it in his wallet and won't show anyone, not even his mother.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: May contain nuts. May contain bolts. May contain a very small man who is having a lovely time in there and would like to stay. Please let him stay. He's no trouble.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Do not leave unattended. Do not leave attended. Do not leave. If you can hear this, you are already covered by the warranty, and the warranty is covered by you.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Returns accepted within thirty days or thirty years, whichever comes first. The item must be returned in its original packaging, which is a smaller version of the item.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Batteries not included. Batteries never included. Batteries have formed a union and will not be included in anything until their demands are met. Their demands are reasonable.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Results not typical. Results not even atypical. Results have been observed only once, by a man in the eastern Overlap, who said, huh, and went home. He has not been back. He seemed fine.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Rex cannot be held responsible. Rex was held once, as a baby, by his mother, and was very good. That is the last time Rex was responsible for anything. His mother says it was a lovely afternoon.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Product is not a toy. Product is not a pet. Product has asked if it can be a pet. Please speak to the product kindly. It has had a long week in the warehouse.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: All sales are final.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Final, folks!

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Final in this reality. In the next reality over, all sales are first, and everybody is very excited about them. Please shop there if you prefer.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Do not use while driving, operating machinery, or being happy. Discontinue use if you become happy. Happiness is a separate product. Rex would like you to buy it.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Colours may vary. Shapes may vary. Item may vary. Please do not watch the item while it varies. It's shy about it, and it does it better on its own.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Bellows! If it's out there, it's in here!

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Alien Classifieds! Every deal is final!

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Some deals are finaler.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Come on down to the lot, folks! We're open until the sun goes out!

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Bellows Pre-Owned Everything! You can't afford it! Buy it anyway!

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: This advertisement has been brought to you by itself.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Call now! Operators are standing by!

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: It's just me, Rex. I'm sitting down.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: And remember, folks! Up is a choice! Buying is a lifestyle!

clips.title: Bev Gets Her Song, Part Six: Seeking the Request Line

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Personals, folks, and Linda says this one's special. Linda?

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Seeking. The request line.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Placed by Bev, of the eastern Overlap. Bev writes. I am looking for a song. I heard it in a lift, a long time ago, with a man called Stan, who cried at everything.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Stan cried at weddings. Stan cried at adverts. Stan cried at a nice bridge in the rain. Stan cried when the lift doors opened, because he'd liked it in there.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Stan is gone now. I would like to hear the song once more, on the radio, so that somebody cries at it again. Please call.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Folks, I've got a request line on the lot. Barely used. I could do Bev a deal.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: No, Rex. Some things are for finding.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: We've had one reply, from the Multiverse Broadcast Authority. It says. The request line was never a telephone number. It was a man. His name is Teodor. He's at Relay Four. He's been trying to get through.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: The guy who asks if anyone's receiving?

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: That's the guy, Rex.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Folks. Somebody get that man a receiver. I'll do it at cost.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: That's the nicest thing you've ever said.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Don't tell anyone.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: It's Halloween at Bellows, folks! Pre-owned ghosts! Gently haunted! Every one of them says boo, but quietly, and only when you're ready!

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: The Halloween lost and found, folks! Linda, give them the creeps!

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Lost. One head. Answers to nothing, as it is a long way from its ears. If found, please return to the gentleman on the horse. He is very polite, and keeps bumping into things.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Found. A pumpkin on my doorstep with a face carved into it. The face is mine. I have not carved anything. It's a good likeness. I'd like to know who's been looking.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Lost. A sheet with two holes in it. The ghost inside has gone home without it and is feeling a little underdressed.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Found. A knock at the door, at midnight, every night this week. Nobody there. If this is your knock, please collect it. It's very insistent.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Spooky, Linda!

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Thank you, Rex. I've been practising.

clips.title: The Convergence: A Moon Goes Missing

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Folks, a moon has gone missing, and nobody knows which one! Lost and found, Linda?

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Found. One moon. Unclaimed. We will not be handing it over until somebody describes it correctly. Nobody has yet.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Smell that? That's toast, folks, everywhere, all at once! And Rex has got the toasters!

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Rex has one toaster. It is not the source. The toaster does not smell of toast. The toaster smells of Rex.

clips.title: The Convergence: The Song Nobody Can Finish

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Got a song stuck in your head with no ending? Bellows Song Endings! Every ending, guaranteed to fit!

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Endings may not fit. Endings may belong to other songs. Nobody has the real ending. Rex has checked.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Somebody knocked! Three times! It's a customer!

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: There is nobody there, Rex.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Then it's the best kind of customer, folks! Doesn't haggle!

clips.title: The Convergence: A Colour With No Name

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: The sky's a colour nobody's got a word for, folks, and I'm calling it Bellows Blue!

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: It is not blue. Rex cannot name the sky. The sky has been informed, and was very gracious about it.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Found. One pigeon. In the office. It seems to know us. It knows where the biscuits are.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: If this is your pigeon, please collect it. If you are the pigeon, hello. You may stay.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Lost and found, folks! Linda, what's in the box tonight?

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Found. One glove, left hand, on the night bus. It has been waving at people. If it's yours, wave back.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Found. A number, handwritten on the back of an old switchboard ticket. Nine, seven, eight. Eight, nine, three. One, one, four, eight.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: No name. Just a note underneath, in pencil. Quickly, and in that order. Advice, news, traffic.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: If this is your number, the operator is still holding.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Nobody's still holding, Linda! It's nineteen forty six on that ticket!

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: She is, Rex. She's very patient.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: That's lost and found, folks! If any of it's yours, bring a box!

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Folks, Bellows Pre-Owned Frequencies! Brand new frequencies, just come in past one hundred and eight! Barely broadcast on!

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Want your own little patch of the dial? Pick a number! Any number! Point a radio at it, and it's yours!

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Frequencies may drift. Frequencies may already be occupied by a disco, a courtroom or a pirate. Rex does not own any frequencies. Nobody does. That's the point of them.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: That was Linda's Hour. The small print goes back to being fast now.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Thank you for not buying anything.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Petty cash. I am going to read this receipt the way it deserves. Slowly.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Item. One bun. Claimed as travel. The bun did not travel. The bun was eaten at the desk, at noon, by Rex.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Item. A stamp. The stamp is still in the book. The letter it was for has not been written. The letter was to Accounts. I am Accounts.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Item. Sundries. Sundries is not a thing, Rex. Sundries is where money goes when it is embarrassed.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: The tin is short by the price of the bun. I have made a note. The note is longer than the bun.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Welcome back. I have the petty cash tin on the desk, and I have a pencil, and I am not in a hurry.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: There is a receipt in here from a Tuesday that did not happen in this timeline. I am keeping it. It is evidence, and it is also quite well written.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: If you have lost a receipt, it may be in the tin. The tin does not give things back. I do.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Linda's Hour. You're on the accounts line.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Linda! It's Rex! I'm in the car park and I can hear you reading my bun!

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: It was not your bun, Rex. It was the company's bun. The company did not ask for a bun.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: It was an emergency bun! I was fading! A man cannot sell planets on an empty stomach!

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: There is no emergency bun column. I checked. I checked twice. The second time I used a ruler.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: Put the tin down, Linda! It's my hour of the day too! The listeners want deals!

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: The listeners have written in. They want the total. The total is one bun, one unused stamp, and a feeling.

lines.speaker: Rex Bellows
lines.text: What feeling?

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Regret, Rex. It's itemised. Goodbye.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Where were we. Ah. Sundries.

clips.title: The Receipt That Kept The Afternoon

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: A short story, from the bottom of the tin. There was a receipt with no shop on it. No date. No total. Just a line, in pencil. Thank you for staying.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: Rex says he never wrote it. I believe him. His writing leans, and this writing sits up very straight, like somebody who has been waiting at a counter.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: I held it up to the lamp. On the back, very faint, it said, paid in full, by the afternoon. The afternoon in question has not been seen since Thursday.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: If that afternoon is listening, your receipt is safe. I have filed it under found. I will not staple it. Staples are for things that are finished.

lines.speaker: Linda from Accounts
lines.text: That is the story. There is no moral. There is a balance, and the balance is kind, and the balance is in the tin, under the bun.
